short: The United Kingdom and France declared war on Germany following the invasion of Poland.
full:
On 3 September 1939, two days after German forces invaded Poland, the United Kingdom and France declared war on Germany. Neville Chamberlain announced the British declaration in a radio broadcast at 11:15 a.m. after an ultimatum demanding German withdrawal expired unanswered. The French declaration followed at 5:00 p.m. the same day.

These declarations marked the formal beginning of the Second World War in Europe. Both nations immediately began mobilising their armed forces and enacting emergency measures. The United Kingdom established a naval blockade of Germany, while France initiated a limited offensive into the Saarland, though large-scale land operations on the Western Front would not begin until the following spring.
